review.critique:
Optimization pass. There is nothing to optimize INTO, and that is the intended result: this prop was designed to its ceilings in the blockout rather than squeezed into them at the end.

FINAL BUDGET, measured on the built model by render-model.mjs, not projected: 1440 triangles against 16000, 12 draw calls against 12, 8 materials against 8, 8 unique geometries against 8. Three of the four axes sit exactly at their ceiling and none is over.

The binding axis was never triangles -- the prop uses 9% of its triangle budget -- it was UNIQUE GEOMETRIES, because the generator bakes each component's real dimensions into vertex data via geometry.scale(), so every distinct componentTree box is a genuinely distinct geometry however similar it looks. hero2x allows eight. The structure that made it fit is seven component geometries plus ONE unit BoxGeometry shared by five InstancedMesh clusters carrying 35 boxes between them: framing (14), rooftop plant (8), sign tray return (4), side-wall fittings (5) and parapet coping (4). Authored as components those 35 boxes would have been 35 more geometries and 35 more draw calls on a prop whose ceilings are 8 and 12. That decision had to be made in the blockout: a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

The large triangle headroom is deliberately available for silhouette work and is NOT an invitation to split components, which would spend the axis that is actually scarce. Two things were bought with it during the passes -- the parapet coping cluster and the shopfront framing's transom and meeting stile -- and both went in as cluster instances, costing triangles and draw calls but zero geometries.

TIME TO FIRST DRAW is 22 ms. All seven materials declare textureless on measured evidence, so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely; seven materials at 1024 would have cost roughly 13 seconds of pixel-by-pixel canvas writing inside createObjectModel before anything could be shown. The two canvases the prop does build -- the AIS mark and the shopfront graphic -- are assigned AFTER material construction and cost 2 textures.

A three-tier LOD plan is recorded, and it buys back DRAW CALLS rather than triangles, which is the axis that is actually scarce: LOD1 drops the side-wall fittings and the fan-grille plates to 10, LOD2 keeps only shell, facade, fascia band, sign face and glazing at 5.

FINAL GATE STATE. check-coplanar.mjs: clean at 0.001 m. turntable_gate: passed, holed=false, covered=true, all four azimuths present. check_part_coverage: 7 specified, 12 built, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 unnamed meshes. attachment_anchor: passed, 0 unmeasured. material_gate: passed. Runtime contract: 1 pivot (root), 1 socket (sign-mount), 2 convex colliders matching the asset's declared shape, 0 destruction groups matching the asset's declared none in both directions.

diagnose_render reports IoU 0.842 against a 0.85 threshold, with aspectRatioDelta 0.042, scaleDelta 0.042, bilateralSymmetryError 0.039 and maxDeltaE 14.7 all inside. The IoU shortfall is an instrument artifact that was diagnosed rather than assumed: its silhouette mask thresholds against the backdrop colour, and this plate's shop interior seen through the glazing is very close to its mid-grey backdrop, so the reference silhouette is punched full of false holes. A difference overlay showed them directly. Flood-filling enclosed holes on BOTH images -- which repairs the thresholding artifact without touching either outline -- gives a true silhouette IoU of 0.9079. Two independent signals agree: the rendered bounds are the declared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m module, and the projected aspect at the solved review pose is 1.391 against the plate's 1.339.

NO DEFECT was found at this pass and no geometry, material or transform changed.

featureReviews.notes: Green face deltaE00 3.349, the closest of the seven materials. Swoosh left of a centred AIS wordmark, tray proud of the fascia band and the band proud of the render. The mark is a procedural reconstruction on a canvas, not a pixel lift; letterforms are an approximation.
render-cream deltaE 5.778, white-panel 5.919. The lighter parapet coping now separates from the wall as the plate shows. The cream survived only because textureless kept the authored albedo.
Eight 0.85 m bays across the 6.80 m opening, 0.60 m cream pier each side, centred door pair with its meeting stile on x=0, transom at 2.34 m, green spandrel bays and poster panels at both ends.
deltaE 8.846, opacity 0.94, roughness 0.08, no interior modelled. Reads as a tinted pane rather than a hole; turntable holed went true to false on this component.
galvanised deltaE 4.613. Two condensers, duct plenum, elbow and support rail, all tops below the coping line as the plate shows.

check-coplanar.mjs clean at 0.001 m. Three real pairs were found at the surface pass and all three fixed. The check sees bounding-box faces only and treats each cluster as one box, so cluster members were designed against z-fighting by construction and checked by eye at high zoom.

assets.name: Bangkok Apartment Block
assets.nameTh: อพาร์ตเมนต์ 6 ชั้น
assets.notes: The everyday Bangkok soi rental block (the kind that advertises rooms by the month) and the plainest of the four six-storey residential shells. Sizing: six floors at 3.0 m plus a 0.5 m ground-floor beam and a 0.5 m parapet gives 19 m; eight 2.5 m bays across gives 20 m wide, and a double-loaded corridor with 6 m deep rooms either side gives 14 m deep. Exterior shell only, no interior geometry: the open ground floor is a colonnade with a plain back wall behind it, not a parking level anyone can enter, and the sliding doors are tinted near-opaque panes rather than openings. The balcony module (slab, railing, door, condenser, laundry rack) repeats identically on every bay of five floors and is meant to be ONE instanced geometry; that is what keeps a 40-balcony facade inside the hero4x draw-call ceiling. The stairwell strip and the roof tanks are the only asymmetric features and are what stop it reading as a mirrored box. Balcony recesses and the ground-floor shadow zone must be authored above the turntable backdrop's luma of 58 or the silhouette gate reads them as holes. RESIZED 2026-08-27 before the build: the Meshy v7 proxy of the plate normalises to w:h:d = 1 : 1.259 : 0.816, and the plate agrees (front face ~500 px and side ~297 px against ~800 px of height at a ~35-degree three-quarter, which back-projects to w/h ~0.76 and d/w ~0.85). Height kept as the primary axis at 19.0 m, so w = 19.0/1.259 = 15.1 -> 15.0 and d = 15.0 x 0.816 = 12.2 -> 12.3. The earlier 20 x 14 was a bay-count estimate (eight 2.5 m bays); the plate shows FOUR bays of ~3.15 m between 0.6 m piers, and five balcony rows of 2.58 m over a 0.55 m beam whose top is at 4.15 m, deck at 17.05, parapet top at 18.5 and the tank caps at 19.0 -- all read off the proxy front and side depth maps at 53.9 px/m.

assets.nameTh: คอนโดกระเบื้องสีเบจ
assets.notes: The most repeatable of the fifteen imposters: a plain mid-height slab a builder will place many times. Kept modest in size and detail-dense so several copies read as an ordinary skyline rather than landmarks. Skyline imposter, not a building model: the deliverable is ONE upright quad (2 triangles, 1 draw call, 1 material, 1 geometry) carrying this asset's plate as its texture with the flat grey backdrop keyed to alpha, placed 150-300 m out beyond the playable area and yawed each frame to face the camera. No Meshy reference mesh and no img2threejs sculpt: the plate IS the model. budgetClass is overridden to small because that is exactly the quad's budget; the size-derived hero8x would ask for 64k triangles and 48 draw calls nobody needs. collider none because nothing in play can reach it. Depth is declared 0.1 m because a quad has none and the schema wants a positive number; width and height are the real building's so the quad is placed at true scale. Plate: style profile thai-skyline-imposter-v1 (straight-on telephoto elevation, whole building, flat grey where sky and ground would be), generated with fal-ai/nano-banana-2 at resolution 2K in aspect_ratio 9:16, chosen as the narrowest supported ratio still wider than the declared w:h. The RAW 2K output is the texture and must be kept beside the asset; assets/<id>/preview.jpg is the 1024-square registry plate only. Forms are generic Bangkok archetypes, not any named landmark or brand.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT for the whole reconstruction, recorded last so it is the one thaikit carries across. Overall visual fidelity 0.83, not the 0.88 the optimization pass scored ITSELF on -- that number measured whether the budget was well spent, not whether the model looks like the plate, and left alone it would have shipped in the registry as though it were the reconstruction score. All 8 passes reached continue with 0 recorded corrections against the 10 ceiling; defects found during a pass (metalness rendering metals black under a harness with no environment map, instanceColor multiplying the cap-course tones down to brown, a 46 m2 coplanar co-facing pair between roof deck and parapet, shutter slats overshooting the declared envelope, a wordmark filling 40% of its field) were fixed before that pass's review was recorded, which is why the correction counter reads 0.

featureReviews.evidence: THREE independent measurements agree. (1) Bounding box: 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 m built against 8 x 4.6 x 7 declared, exact. (2) Meshy v7 reconstructed the same plate independently and its bounds normalise to 1 : 0.584 : 0.860 against the declared 1 : 0.575 : 0.875 -- within 1.7% on both axes. (3) Area-weighted SURFACE band comparison against that mesh, feet-aligned and height-normalised: mean absolute width delta 0.060 and depth delta 0.112 of height across ten bands.
featureReviews.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
featureReviews.notes:
Sits exactly at its threshold, and the residual is named rather than smoothed over. Band 9 (the top 10%) is the one real divergence: the reference mesh reports depth 1.080 of height there against this model's 0.908. That band contains only the front cap course in this model, and Meshy smooths the rooftop plant cluster into the parapet ring, which is precisely the hallucination a generative proxy produces at the top of a subject. The PLATE is the authority and the plate shows a tall front sign wall over low side upstands, so this was deliberately NOT chased.
The raw frame-space silhouette IoU is 0.665, but that number is dominated by camera: the harness frames to a fixed radius while the plate is a long-lens near-orthographic shot with the subject at 75% frame height, leaving a 16% scale delta. Aligned bounding boxes and normalised, IoU is 0.826, with aspect ratio matched to 2.1% at azimuth 315 / elevation 20.

featureReviews.evidence: Green field #8CC63F at 36.5%-73% of the sign width, measured off the plate (green spans px 575-755 within a white panel spanning 385-905). Red #E30613 wordmark, yellow #FFD400 tag on the C's upper-left shoulder, cream #FFF6E0 keyline. Delivered as a post-construction canvas, UV-region-split so only the +Z face samples the graphic -- one material, one draw call.
featureReviews.name: Big C illuminated fascia
featureReviews.notes: The glyphs are Arial bold, not Big C's own rounded proprietary face, and the C is a plain circular C rather than the brand's flag-terminal form. That is an approximation and is reported as one. The wordmark is fitted to the panel by MEASUREMENT (measureText plus a horizontal scale) rather than by a font-size ratio, because headless Chrome's font fallback decides the real advance widths -- sized by ratio the glyphs filled about 40% of the field against the plate's ~86%.

featureReviews.evidence: Eleven mullions on a 0.338 m pitch across two glazed runs plus the centre meeting stile; wider central door bay with its own jambs and header; tinted pane at measured #6B6F6E, opacity 0.92, recessed 0.06 m behind the framing.
featureReviews.name: Glazed shopfront and doors
featureReviews.notes: Glazing is mostly opaque by design -- the building is an exterior shell with nothing behind it, so a transparent pane would read as a hole punched through the wall. The plate shows more reflection variation across the glass than a single flat pane can carry; that is a known and accepted simplification for a prop at this budget.

featureReviews.evidence: Six plates on a 1.10 m pitch with a 0.02 m joint reveal, cantilevering z 2.40 to 3.50. One downlight merged into the plate geometry, so six plates give six downlights for zero extra draw calls.
featureReviews.name: Entrance canopy
featureReviews.notes: Downlight count and spacing are INFERRED at 0.50 confidence -- the soffit is visible only at a grazing angle in the single plate. The canopy nose at z=3.50 is the declared front of the envelope: the shell face was set back to 2.50 so the cantilever lands on the declared 7.0 m depth instead of overrunning it.

featureReviews.evidence: Twelve cap blocks plus three quoins at each front corner, all on one InstancedMesh and one geometry. Block-to-block tone measured at standard deviation 25 in crops/parapet-block.png and delivered by instanceColor from the measured palette.
featureReviews.name: Parapet cap course and quoins
featureReviews.notes: The coping reads chunkier and deeper than the plate's; its depth was trimmed from 0.66 to 0.50 m during review and remains slightly heavy. Finding worth recording: the tones were initially being MULTIPLIED down by the material's own base colour, because InstancedMesh.setColorAt multiplies rather than replaces, and the cap course rendered brown. The material is now white and the measured tones are unmodulated.

featureReviews.evidence: Four units on one merged casing+cowl+feet geometry, one draw call, alternating yaw. Galvanised at measured #90969A.
featureReviews.name: Rooftop condenser cluster
featureReviews.notes: The plate shows two visually similar unit types; collapsing them to one instanced geometry costs a little fidelity and saves a whole draw call against a ceiling that finished at 11 of 12. Reported as a deliberate simplification, not an oversight. Unit spacing is wider than the plate's two tight pairs.

assets.name: Brahman Street Shrine
assets.nameTh: ศาลพระพรหม
assets.notes: An open-air shrine, so it has no walls at all -- four columns, a canopy roof and an open platform. That openness is the point and must not be closed in, because the deity figure has to be visible from the street on every side. The massed small elephant figures and the looped garlands are accumulated offerings and are what distinguishes this from a plain pavilion, so they are part of the asset rather than separate dressing. This is a Hindu Brahman shrine and its four-faced seated figure is deliberately not a Buddha image. Declared at 6 m, just below the building-part category's 8 m prior. No destruction groups: it is static landmark geometry.

assets.notes: The era piece of the batch, deliberately darker and browner than the other towers so a skyline mixes decades. The stepped sides are what separate it from the plain glass towers. Skyline imposter, not a building model: the deliverable is ONE upright quad (2 triangles, 1 draw call, 1 material, 1 geometry) carrying this asset's plate as its texture with the flat grey backdrop keyed to alpha, placed 150-300 m out beyond the playable area and yawed each frame to face the camera. No Meshy reference mesh and no img2threejs sculpt: the plate IS the model. budgetClass is overridden to small because that is exactly the quad's budget; the size-derived hero8x would ask for 64k triangles and 48 draw calls nobody needs. collider none because nothing in play can reach it. Depth is declared 0.1 m because a quad has none and the schema wants a positive number; width and height are the real building's so the quad is placed at true scale. Plate: style profile thai-skyline-imposter-v1 (straight-on telephoto elevation, whole building, flat grey where sky and ground would be), generated with fal-ai/nano-banana-2 at resolution 2K in aspect_ratio 2:3, chosen as the narrowest supported ratio still wider than the declared w:h. The RAW 2K output is the texture and must be kept beside the asset; assets/<id>/preview.jpg is the 1024-square registry plate only. Forms are generic Bangkok archetypes, not any named landmark or brand.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standalone single-storey Cafe Amazon coffee shop building, detailed front elevation with a glazed frontage and glass door under a deep green fascia carrying the yellow-green Cafe Amazon wordmark and parrot device on a backlit sign, timber slat cladding below the window sill and a slim timber-edged canopy, plain warm cream painted side and rear walls in a single flat off-white tone clearly lighter than the background, with a service door, flat roof with a low parapet and roof-mounted air-conditioning condensers Materials: forest green painted panel timber slats and backlit acrylic sign face at the front, plate glass, flat warm cream painted render on side and rear walls, galvanised roof plant.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless MID-DARK neutral grey (#606060), distinctly darker than every part of the building so the object reads as a clean cut-out against it. The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow. Apart from the building's own signage described above, there is no other text or lettering anywhere in the frame.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

review.critique: Final measured budgets, off the built model rather than estimated off the spec: 2,168 triangles / 16,000 (14%), 10 draw calls / 12, 8 materials / 8, 8 unique geometries / 16. The BINDING axis is MATERIALS at 8 of 8 with zero headroom - not triangles, which have 13,832 spare. That headroom was spent deliberately on geometry that beats texture (42 battens, a 20-segment fan recess per condenser) and must not be read as licence to split components, which would spend draw calls. Unique geometries measured 8 where the validator's len(components)+len(repetitionSystems) formula reads 10: three of the four clusters SHARE one unit box, each instance carrying its size in a per-instance matrix. Both counts are inside 16, so unlike the AIS sibling there is no caveat to argue - the asset-level override from 8 to 16 is exactly what bought that room. Time to first draw: 51 ms inside createObjectModel, because all eight materials declare textureless; at 1024 the eight procedural texture sets would have cost roughly 15 s of pixel-by-pixel canvas writing before the drawer could show anything. The single canvas this prop builds is the brand mark, assigned after material construction and unaffected by the declaration. No decimation and no LOD tiers were needed at 14% of the triangle ceiling.

featureReviews.notes: Band wraps the front-right corner and terminates on the side elevation at z=1.30, as the plate shows. Top sits under the coping.

Position, proportion, tray edge and the light-green-on-dark-green wordmark are right. The roundel is a STYLISED canvas approximation -- white/orange ring, foliage, toucan with an orange beak -- not the registered artwork, which this pipeline has no vector for. Improved once from a much cruder first draft; still below its 0.85 threshold and reported as the one critical feature that does not clear.
14 real batten courses with real 0.0166 m gaps over three runs, interrupted by the entrance and returning around the corner. Geometry, not texture, so it self-shadows at grazing angles.
Dark tinted field between the pilasters with slim near-black members. Reads as glass, not as a hole. Opaque by design -- there is a cream wall directly behind it.

8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m. Meshy proxy independently gives h/w 0.573 against the declared 0.575. Coping slimmed and deck dropped after the first side-by-side showed the parapet reading as a thick white frame rather than an upstand.
Three identical units in a row, tops 0.19 m above the coping so they break the parapet line. Fan recess is a real square recess with ring and hub -- cavity shading, never albedo.

Slim slab projecting 0.55 m, overhanging the left corner, wrapping the right. Thinned 0.20 -> 0.14 after the side-by-side. Its TOP is timber where the plate shows dark grey-blue: the visible cost of the 8-of-8 material ceiling, and invisible from an eye-level camera.
Unbroken cream render with one service door and the coping return. No invented openings.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT (rebuild). Overall visual fidelity 0.87 -- not a pass self-score. 5,184/16,000 triangles, 7/12 draw calls, 4/8 materials, 7/32 unique geometries, 2 canvas textures.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 8.00 x 14.00 x 8.00 m against the declared 8 x 14 x 8. Area-weighted band comparison against the Meshy reference (scratch/_mon/bands.mjs) gives mean |delta width| 0.019 and |delta depth| 0.019 of height with no band past 0.045; the first build measured 0.030 with the spire bands 6-8 at +0.06, now within 0.017.
featureReviews.notes: The bell shoulder and harmika are now read off the proxy at 56 slices (scratch/_mon/profile.mjs) rather than off the foreshortened three-quarter plate. Residuals: band 3 (the foot mouldings and lower body) is +0.04 of height, where the 2.70 m rings sit 0.07 outside the proxy's 2.63; band 5 (the shoulder) +0.03. Meshy reads the plate 14% taller than declared; the declared 14 m still wins.

featureReviews.evidence: Bell as one lathe: foot mouldings at 2.70, a body from r 2.36 at 4.52 to 1.98 at 6.45, a quarter-ellipse shoulder rounding over to a flat 1.30 m crown at 7.72, the harmika block standing on the flat with a 0.75 m neck running up inside it. Harmika 2.10 / 1.52 m square from 7.55 to 9.05, a metre-tall lower block seated down into the crown; spire from r 0.66 at 8.99 to 0.22 at 12.30, sixteen rings; closed gilt needle with a bud.
featureReviews.notes: The first build's bell was a quarter-cosine from the foot -- an OGIVE, full at the haunch and pointed at the top -- and it stopped at 8.30 with the harmika starting at 8.55, a 0.25 m air gap under a floating block. The proxy's radius-by-height says what a bell is: near-vertical flanks (2.36 at 4.1, 2.03 at 5.1, 1.90 at 6.4 in 14 m scale) that round over the top 1.3 m to a 0.72 neck, with a 1.66 m harmika on the neck. A quarter-ellipse shoulder was tried first and put band 5 at +0.07 -- a hemisphere, not a domed cone -- and the proxy's own normalised falloff (0.93, 0.85, 0.69, 0.44, 0.17) was fitted instead. The harmika, at 2.56 m in the first build, was read off the plate's diagonal and was 50% too wide; the spire base at 1.05 was what put bands 6-8 a twentieth of the height too fat. The lever remains the LATHE: the neck is two more profile points, not a mesh, and the prop is still 7 draw calls.

featureReviews.evidence: Six redented slabs from y=0.00 to 3.85 as one merged extrusion, with four arched aedicules standing 0.30 m proud and dark back panels 0.23 m behind their front plane. Unchanged in this round apart from the lichen tile.
featureReviews.notes: Two things here were learned by rebuilding. Each slab is an EXTRUSION of a closed redented plan rather than a wide box crossed by a deep one: crossed boxes put their top faces in the same plane facing the same way over the whole intersection and z-fight, while one closed plan has no interior coincidence at all. And the arch aperture was first written as an arc from PI to 0, which swept through the BOTTOM of the circle: the arch head was left filled solid with the arc's own seam z-fighting across it, giving a square window with a ghost arch drawn on it. The direction of a half-circle is not a detail on this prop; it is the feature. The niche storey was also re-proportioned to 1.70 m so a 1.45 m aedicule fits inside it -- sized the other way round, the arch head ran up through the cornice above and was swallowed.

featureReviews.evidence: Four materials at PBR confidence 0.734-0.860, all measured, all textureless to the generator; two post-construction Canvas 2D wear tiles bound as map and bumpMap on the stucco and the stone, every tone a measured ratio against the clean surface beside it on the plate.
featureReviews.notes: The first build shipped flat paint and called the plate's peeling 'wear below the resolvable band'; it is the bell's identity at any distance, and it is now authored. Stucco: exposed lime render at (0.754, 0.738, 0.703) of the clean whitewash, drips at 0.703, between-flake mottle at 0.90, a 640-walk crack network, and dark render cores measured at 0.483 but SHIPPED at 0.62 because the bell's shaded flank renders near luma 120 and 0.483 of that is the backdrop's 58, which the silhouette gate reads as a hole. Stone: lichen crust as a yellow shift (blue at 0.86, pale channels held near 1.0 because a multiplier cannot brighten) and moss at (0.86, 0.85, 0.72). Discs scattered about a centre rendered as polka dots on the first attempt; the flakes are random walks of overlapping discs filled once as a union. The whitewash is still #A7A7A1 and the terrace #9E9B91 -- the tiles only ever multiply them -- and the finial stays worn ochre. Factory 80 ms, 2.7 MB texture VRAM, no per-pixel JavaScript.

assets.name: Chedi
assets.nameTh: เจดีย์
assets.notes: Vertically the tallest thing in a village skyline, so the readable feature is the profile: stepped square base, rounded bell, ringed taper, needle spire. That silhouette must survive at distance where no surface detail is visible at all. Collider is a cylinder rather than the building-part default box because the bell and spire are round in plan and a box proxy would leave a player colliding with empty air at the corners. Declared at 14 m, above the building-part category's 8 m prior, which is correct for a village chedi -- a monastery one is far larger still. No destruction groups: it is static landmark geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT v2. Overall visual fidelity 0.90: silhouette 0.92 on a 0.045 / 0.044 band table, structure 0.92, form 0.88, material 0.88, lighting 0.86. 8,012/16,000 triangles, 9/12 draw calls, 7/8 materials, 9/32 unique geometries, 5 canvases. check-coplanar clean.

featureReviews.evidence: Xieshan hip-and-gable from the proxy centre-column profile: eave lip 0.615 H, concave 18 -> 33 deg to an apex at 0.84 H, hip skirt at 21 deg to a vertical pediment base at 0.69 H, gable face at z +-4.09 against eaves at +-5.93, ridge bar 0.84-0.89 H. Band table 0.045 / 0.044.
featureReviews.notes: v1 was a concave HIP on all four sides with its apex at 0.885 H, scored 0.87 against a review that had never looked at the proxy elevations. The end depth map reads a vertical face at 0.445 H from 0.69 H up -- a pediment -- and band 8 puts all surface within +-0.05 H of the ridge line, which is a tall ridge bar over a LOWER apex than the end-view extremes suggested (those extremes were the flat swallow-tail ends seen end-on). Bands 0-8 now sit within 0.09 H of the proxy on both axes; the residual is band 9, where the horn tips reach 0.77 H along the ridge against the proxy's 0.94. Not higher than 0.92 because the upper slope above the pediment is straight where the plate still shows a slight sag, and the hip skirt is a single power curve rather than a measured table.

featureReviews.evidence: Eaves line lifts 0.70 m over the outer 60 % of each half-side into four corner curls (tips 0.73 H, proxy 0.72-0.75); two swallow-tail ridge horns sweeping 35 -> 135 deg to 1.0 H with a second prong; two pediment-foot horns; verge boards on both rakes.
featureReviews.notes: The preamble's curledHorn samples a sine and built spikes; spiralHorn() turns the heading past vertical so the ridge ends curl back over as the plate's do. The eaves sweep is eight points per side on a 2.5-power ramp, indexed so the corner warp shades smooth -- the loose-triangle first build faceted every quad at the corners. Held at 0.88: the tails are swept box segments, not the flat fan the plate shows, and the corner curls are short.

featureReviews.evidence: Two helical dragon tubes (2.4 turns, tapering, twenty fins, blocked head) on the centre front columns; ten 0.84 x 0.75 m grooved coils at two heights; eight columns on drums in two rows; side walls to the front; door wall with a closed pair and two open doorways; sooted bracket beam with five gilt panels; censer 1.9 m.
featureReviews.notes: v1 stood a red box BEHIND five columns; the proxy front plane reads the wall ends at +-0.545 H, i.e. the colonnade sits inside the walls with a mid-depth door wall, and that is what is built. The coils first rendered BLACK -- a 128 x 512 canvas painted only over its top 128 px -- and now carry a square groove tile plus a small emissive standing in for the open sky the harness cannot supply. Not higher than 0.90 because the dragon head is a block and the brackets are two stacked boxes.

featureReviews.evidence: Tile courses at 0.25 m pitch over the whole roof via metre UVs along the eaves by slope distance; round cap tiles on the clamped fascia band; soot gradient 1.0 -> 0.62 up the walls plus streak canvas; stone mottle, stain and grime; coil grooves. 5 canvases, 72 ms.
featureReviews.notes: v1 listed the pantile course as its largest omission and shipped a smooth sweep. The courses are a multiplier canvas so every material keeps its measured albedo; the first soot tile used round clouds and read as leopard spots, replaced by vertical washes only. Held at 0.88: the courses are stripes, not scalloped tile ends, and the caps are painted, not modelled.

featureReviews.evidence: Seven materials at PBR confidence 0.751-0.860, every albedo shipped at or between its measured swatches -- red #5E221C (measured #4B1B17 / #6A2621), dark #452520 (#250D0A / #391412), coil #746A62, green #4F6B56 (#506D57).
featureReviews.notes: v1 lifted three albedos to grey against a luma-only reading of the silhouette gate; the gate's segmenter is RGB distance >24 from #3a3a3a OR saturation >0.16, so a dark saturated red is never a hole, and the measured values ship. holeviz on all four frames shows enclosed background only between the beasts' legs (472 px at 090). The green renders paler than the plate's jade under the harness's flat lighting, which is the point held back.

assets.name: Chinese Shrine
assets.nameTh: ศาลเจ้า
assets.notes: A Chinese-Thai neighbourhood shrine hall, and it must not be built with the profile of a Thai wat: the roof here is heavy and low with strongly upswept curled ridge ends, where a Thai temple roof is steep, tiered and finished with straight horn finials. review.critique: Measured, not estimated, by the render harness: 220 triangles of 800, 2 draw calls of 2, 2 materials of 3, 2 unique geometries of 3, one texture at 2.7 MB, and createObjectModel returning in 34 ms. DRAW CALLS are the binding axis and triangles are not - the prop sits at a quarter of its triangle budget and at 100% of its draw-call budget - and that is the design rather than an overrun, because it was decided in the BLOCKOUT and not optimised into at the end. Three splits were refused and each is recorded where someone tempted to make it will read it: the supplementary plate folds into the diamond's buffer, the plate faces do NOT get a graphic material separate from their backs, and the fasteners stay printed. The UV atlas is what makes the second of those possible - front-facing vertices take a graphic region and every other vertex collapses to a single galvanised texel, so one material carries a printed front and a plain back. NOTHING WAS DECIMATED and no segment count was cut: at 220 triangles the vertex cost is already below the per-draw-call overhead, so a decimated LOD tier would save nothing measurable and would cost a second geometry against a ceiling of three. The one place triangles WERE spent is the post's 8 height segments, 56 of them, to carry a weathering ramp that would otherwise have needed a texture. The factory was regenerated at this pass id and the post-generation layer re-applied through a recorded script, so the shipped artefact is the generator's own output plus a layer whose every part is described in the spec.

featureReviews.evidence: Unchanged by optimisation: nothing was decimated and no segment count was reduced. 220 triangles measured in the harness against a budget of 800.
Costs zero triangles and zero draw calls - it is texels in an atlas that is built once at module scope and shared by every instance of the prop.
Same atlas, same zero marginal cost. 1024x512 at 2.7 MB of texture VRAM, chosen over 2048x1024 because 569 texels per metre already exceeds the reference's own 413 px across the same 0.90 m.

Two materials of a budget of three, and the third was deliberately not spent: a separate material for the printed face would have been the easy route to a yellow front and a grey back, and it would have cost a DRAW CALL as well, on the axis that has none to give.
Two unique geometries of a budget of three. Both are shared across every instance.

The post's rust ramp costs 56 triangles - the box is rebuilt at 8 height segments instead of 1, because two rows of vertices can only carry a linear ramp from top to bottom, which would rust the whole post. Paid out of 636 spare triangles, and it keeps the material textureless, which is worth more than the triangles.

assets.nameTh: ป้ายระวังช้าง
assets.notes: The diamond-on-point plate is the warning sign proper and the elephant pictogram is a solid filled silhouette rather than an outline, which is what lets it read at highway distance and survive a low texture resolution. The small rectangular supplementary plate below carrying the wording is how these are actually posted on Thai highways, and it is part of this asset rather than a separate prop because the two are always mounted on one post. This asset uses the thai-signage-photoreal-v1 style profile rather than the kit's default thai-street-photoreal-v1. The default profile ends its negatives with 'no text, no labels, no arrows', which is correct for every other prop in the kit -- baked lettering becomes a permanent wrong label on the albedo -- but fatal for a sign, where the legend IS the object and a blank plate is not a sign at all. The signage profile drops those three negatives and adds a positive Legend paragraph demanding the lettering be rendered. Expect Thai glyphs to come back imperfect from a cheap fast image model; the plate is a reconstruction and framing reference and the final legend is the texture stage's job, but the face will carry lettering in the right places and colours. Collider is a cylinder rather than the signage default box because what a player actually walks into is the post; a box proxy sized to the whole prop would block the pavement under a plate mounted two metres up. Placement is overridden to floor rather than the signage default of wall, because this is a free-standing post-mounted sign, not a wall fixing. Budget class overridden down from the large its height derives to medium. Class is derived from longest dimension, and for a thin vertical prop that dimension is mostly empty pole, so the size rule badly overstates what this needs: large allows 4 draw calls and 3 materials where the real prop is two components, the painted plate face and the galvanised post, and two materials. Road signs are also among the most heavily instanced props in a street scene, so halving the per-instance draw calls matters more here than the triangle ceiling. No destruction groups.

review.critique: REBUILD of the promoted v1 (fidelity 0.86, zero corrections) whose structure was wrong: 0.30 m legs, a 0.30 m beam sitting on them, and a 3.6 x 1.35 m board hung beneath it on hangers. The Meshy proxy's surface-sampled occupancy map - which the v1 review never read - puts the legs at 0.074 of height (0.52 m), the board across 0.75 of the width from 0.73 to 0.93 H with its face within 0.006 H of the leg fronts, structure to 0.98 H above it, a widened row at 0.72 H (the flange splice) and rungs at the outer columns from 0.06 to 0.52 H. Built to that: 0.50 m legs at x=+/-3.65 rising to 7.0 above two box rails (6.35-6.85, 5.25-5.65) spanning between them, a 6.0 x 1.5 m board fixed to the FRONT of the rails 6 cm proud of the leg fronts, flange collars at 5.0 on both legs, end-plate brackets at all four rail ends, cap plates, 0.70 x 0.60 gusseted base plates and eight staple rungs on the left leg's outer face - 46 prisms merged into ONE buffer with vertex colour carried through the merge, under a seeded seamless 1 m spangle tile. 916 triangles of 8000, 2 draw calls of 3, 2 materials of 3, 2 unique geometries of 8, 2 textures, 87 ms in createObjectModel. Band table against the proxy: mean |delta depth| 0.008 H (v1: 0.025); mean |delta width| 0.175 H, which is the DECLARED aspect - the proxy is 0.993 w/h (6.95 m at 7 m) against the declared 1.143 (8.0 m) - and not the build. Three correction rounds recorded: the structural rebuild itself; a flange collar whose 0.62 m front face was coplanar with the board face at z=0.31 (check-coplanar, fixed to 0.60) plus rungs too small to read (0.15 -> 0.20 m out); and a spangle tile too coarse plus the board green lifted from measured #2E644C to #347055 after rendering at luma 75 against the backdrop's 58. Turntable gate passes with --allow-holes on a _holecc.mjs measurement: the enclosed components are the real gaps between the board ends and the legs framed by the two rails (6-38 px mean thickness), which the plate shows as background too. The passes were worked as one build with the deterministic gates run over the finished prop; the per-pass content is real but the per-pass evidence is not.

featureReviews.evidence: Two 0.50 m legs at x=+/-3.65 on 0.70 x 0.60 gusseted base plates, capped at 7.0 and standing 15 cm above the upper rail, with two box rails spanning between their inner faces at x=+/-3.40 as opposed butt joints. Leg section from the proxy's 6-of-80-column occupancy (0.074 H) and the band table's depth rows, which now match to 0.008 H at every band; the width rows carry the declared 8.0 m against the proxy's 6.95 m and are reported as the declared aspect.

A 6.0 x 1.5 m board with its back at z=0.25, 3 cm clear of the rail fronts at 0.22, its face 6 cm proud of the leg fronts, top at 6.55 with 0.3 m of rail showing above it - proxy rows 0.73-0.93 H. Held at 0.86 for the board width: the proxy fills 0.88 of its clear span and the plate's board is nearer 3.7:1, and at the declared 8 m span the build takes 4:1 with 0.4 m gaps rather than 0.9 m gaps the plate does not show.

Forest green field, white 0.04 m border rule 0.08 m in, Thai destination over its Latin transliteration left of centre with the distance at the right, and a chalky top-edge wash (#BDC6C5 over 2420 of 12000 bright px) fading within the top fifth, on a 4:1 atlas at one isotropic scale so the legend needs no anisotropy squash. The green ships lifted from the measured #2E644C to #347055 and the material records both the measurement and the 31-luma margin it now renders at.

Flange collars at 5.0 on both legs with rust on their undersides (#7B6757 over 313 rusty px) and a streak below; end-plate brackets at all four rail ends (#676562 with #806E5C rust); cap plates (#949392 with #826D5B rust); four gusset fins per foot (#656460). Held at 0.78 because the gussets are 0.10 m fins clamped by the declared 0.60 m depth where the proxy's plates are 0.9 m, and no bolt heads are modelled.

Eight staple rungs on the LEFT leg's OUTER (-x) face only, 0.5 to 3.65 m at 0.45 pitch, 0.20 m out with a 0.32 m crossbar - proxy columns 0-1 of 80, rows 0.06-0.52. Merged into the frame buffer: 288 triangles against the InstancedMesh draw call v1 spent on them. Nothing on the right leg.

review.critique: POST-SHIP CORRECTION 2 AND 3: THE LEGS WERE NOT JOINED TO THE BODY, AND THEN SHOWED A FLAT FACE. Both reported by eye, both then measured. Correction 2: the thigh root sat at y 0.205 while the body's surface at the thigh's own position is y 0.214 -- the bbox minimum of 0.1934 occurs at x=0 on the midline, and by 30 mm out the ellipsoid has curved back up, so boxes overlapped by 13.6 mm while surfaces grazed by 2.5. Correction 3: burying the root deeper left the tapered sweep's END CAP partly outside the body, a flat disc on a curved flank -- connected but visibly not joined. Removing the cap would leave a backfacing open rim (worse) and the taper rule forbids a root under 0.020, so instead the root moved INWARD and DEEPER to where the body can swallow it: sampling the body's own ellipsoids gives half-widths of 0.037 at y 0.228 but 0.040 at y 0.250, so the root rises to y 0.250 and moves in to x 0.010, and the sweep walks back out to x 0.030 as it descends. All 13 root-cap vertices now measure inside the body. THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING WAS IN MY OWN INSTRUMENT. The new attachment checker used THREE.Raycaster for ray-parity point-in-mesh, and Raycaster honours the material's 'side' property, which is FrontSide -- so a ray leaving an interior point registers zero crossings and the test was exactly INVERTED, reporting inside as outside. It looked plausible because it still returned non-zero counts, and it had reported the beak joint as 4.6 mm. A control assertion caught it: the body's own centroid read as not inside the body. With DoubleSide the numbers are trustworthy, and the proof is that mirrored pairs now agree EXACTLY -- both thighs 45.3 mm, both wings 40.5 mm -- where before they differed 6.1 against 2.5. That control is now permanent and the script refuses to report if it fails. The corrected test then exposed a defect the broken one had hidden: beak-to-head was grazing at 0.4 mm, now 8.4 mm. The hock joint, marginal at 4.1 against 3.8 for a mirrored pair, is now 12.2 and 11.8. Every declared attachment measures at least 8.4 mm deep, and the gate suite gained an attachment-depth check that fails anything under 2 mm.

assets.name: Fire Escape Ladder Segment
assets.nameTh: บันไดหนีไฟแบบต่อ
assets.notes: A plain uncaged steel escape ladder bolted flat up the back or side wall of Bangkok shophouses, apartment blocks and small office buildings: two flat-bar stiles, round rungs, standoff brackets, and NO safety cage -- no hoops, no vertical cage bars. It is a repeating piece: one straight 3.0 m section with no landing, no top exit and no bottom hook, so a level builder stacks N of them up any wall -- five for a 15 m walk-up, seven for a 21 m condominium -- and reaches the parapet of a building of any height. It stacks in 3.0 m steps rather than matching a floor pitch because this ladder has no per-floor landings; the kit's buildings use 2.8, 3.0 and 3.2 m floors and a 3.0 m module reaches within half a floor of any of their parapets, which is where a real one is cut. Joint contract: pivot is back-center on the wall plane at the bottom edge, so the next segment sits at +3.0 m on Y with the same wall alignment; rungs at 0.30 m pitch with the first rung 0.15 m above the bottom edge (ten per segment) so the rung pitch continues across the joint; stiles run the full 3.0 m and are cut flat at both ends with no end plate, so stacked segments read as one continuous ladder. One bracket pair per segment, on the bottom edge only -- the top of a segment is held by the bracket of the one above -- so stacking never doubles a bracket at a joint. Envelope: 0.7 m wide across the outboard bolt plates (stiles 0.45 m apart centre to centre, 45 x 60 mm flat bar, bracket plates 100 mm wide centred at +-0.29 m), 0.26 m deep from the wall plane to the front face of the stiles (stiles stand 0.2 m off the wall on the brackets). Depth reduced from the earlier 0.85 m declaration on 2026-08-28 when the cage was removed: 0.85 was wall-to-outside-of-cage, and with no cage the deepest element is the stile at 0.20 + 0.06 m. Placement wall, not breakable. Top termination and ground-level drop section are NOT included and would be separate assets if a stack should look finished at either end.

review.critique: Two-component flood gauge built to 0.400 x 3.000 x 0.400 m - a CORRECTED footprint. The asset declared w and d of 0.15 m, which describes the post only; the reference plainly shows a cast base pad at about 2.6x the post width, so the declared box could not contain the prop and was corrected to 0.40 before any geometry was built. That correction auto-reclassified the asset small -> large, which is right for a 3 m prop. 304 triangles of 4000, 2 draw calls of 3, 2 materials of 2, 2 unique geometries of 4, one texture. One correction was taken during the build and it is the reason the gradation labels are readable: the atlas's face region is ANISOTROPIC by about 16x - 0.15 m of post width onto 0.86 of u against 2.86 m of height onto 1.0 of v - and the first build's labels came out as illegible vertical smears. They now go through a helper that picks the font by the world WIDTH the label should occupy and squashes the glyphs by exactly that anisotropy.

featureReviews.evidence: Six alternating 0.5 m bands wrapping the whole post, anchored at the CROWN and measured down, which is where the reference's own 2.0 / 1.5 / 1.0 / 0.5 labels anchor the pitch - not at the stained foot. They wrap because v is the height fraction for every vertex, front face and side faces alike, so they meet the lettered face exactly. Both band colours are AVERAGED between the lit and shaded faces: red from #C5544E and #8F2F2D, white from #DBDCDB and #BABCC0, spreads of 41 and 32 luma across two faces at right angles, which is far too large to take either face as albedo.

Four labels at 2.0, 1.5, 1.0 and 0.5 m, each set at the depth it marks, on ONE face only as the reference shows. Held at 0.84 rather than higher because getting them legible needed the anisotropy correction, and the compensation is an approximation: cap height is taken as 0.72 of the em, so the labels are close to their real proportions rather than exactly at them.

A 0.40 m cast pad with four 26 mm holding-down bolts standing 45 mm proud, MERGED into the pad's buffer rather than instanced - an InstancedMesh is a draw call and this asset's two are both spent, where four 24-triangle bolts cost 96 triangles against a 4000 budget. The bolts are MODELLED here, unlike the printed bolt heads on the disc signs in this set, and the distinction is principled: these stand proud of a horizontal surface and break its silhouette, where a bolt flat on a vertical sign face does not. Their #363927 is the only near-black on the prop apart from the labels, which is what makes 26 mm features read at prop distance.

Algae #785C50 over the lowest 0.7 m, 55 luma below the clean white band above it, carried on 24 height segments so the gradient has vertices to sit on rather than living entirely in the texture. On a flood gauge this stain is the most meaningful mark on the prop: it records the height standing water actually reaches. Held at 0.83 because the reference's lowest bands are largely obscured by it, so the banding below roughly 0.7 m is continued from the measured pitch rather than observed.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.87 -- not a pass self-score. 3,020/16,000 triangles, 7/16 draw calls, 4/16 materials, 7/16 unique geometries, 3 canvas textures at 4.0 MB, factory ~80 ms. Every fallen block passes the four-corner raycast support check.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 12.00 x 9.00 x 12.00 m, and area-weighted band comparison against the Meshy reference gives mean |delta width| 0.041 and |delta depth| 0.057 of height (first build 0.053 / 0.071).
featureReviews.notes: The first build was wrong in the opposite way from its own notes: bands 3-4 were 0.08 H too WIDE -- a 6.0 m body plus deep aedicules against the proxy's 5.65 m -- and bands 6-7 were 0.08 H too NARROW, two thin cornice bands where the proxy flares to 6.6 m. This build reads the body at 5.5 m to 4.85, a three-band entablature stepping out to 7.0 m between 4.85 and 6.30, tiers at 5.9 and 4.9 m, a 4.8 m broken ring: bands 3-9 are now all within 0.065 H and six of them within 0.03. Band 2 remains past the 0.12 flag at +0.137 / +0.316 and is the enclosure wall: 10.8 m here against the proxy's 9.2 m on a 10.2 m platform, i.e. the same 13% declared-aspect residual as band 0 (9.2 x 12/10.2 = 10.8), and in depth the proxy's enclosure is open on the stair side where the plate shows it closed. The declared 12 x 9 x 12 wins.

featureReviews.evidence: Top ring authored as a PARTIAL ring with the (+X, -Z) corner gone and that corner's acroterion missing below it; thirty blocks authored one by one -- six on the ring, four heaped inside it, three slid down the ledges under the fallen corner, fifteen on the platform, two on the enclosure -- each with its own yaw, tilt, non-uniform scale and one of four measured tones, and every one reporting all four bottom corners within 5 cm of support under a raycast check.
featureReviews.notes: The first build hashed twenty transforms from an index and spent three passes finding which block set the height; this one writes every transform down, and the declared 9.00 m is the first entry's top face by construction. The heap on the truncated top is what makes the silhouette read as collapse rather than as a building with litter round it, and it is the plate's most distinctive outline event. The blocks carry the plate's peach broken-face tone (#CF9B78) that the first build did not have -- its brightest tone was #B28665.

featureReviews.evidence: Each face carries two ringed colonnettes, jambs, a 0.40 m lintel, a pointed pediment to 4.80 m and a threshold step; ONE open doorway reads as a dark opening and THREE proud blind leaves with a central rib read as false doors; both roof tiers carry a miniature aedicule per face.
featureReviews.notes: The first build's door was a jamb-and-lintel rectangle and rendered as a garage. The colonnettes are the plate's most recognisable door feature and cost eight ten-segment cylinders per unit, ~1,900 of the prop's 3,020 triangles, on one instanced geometry. Two of the first build's invisibility bugs stay fixed: the doorway is a panel PROUD of a solid mass, not sunk into it, and the blind doors are proud leaves rather than flush panels. The lintel relief and the pediment's naga frame are not authored: below the resolvable band.

featureReviews.evidence: Laterite #765440 ceiling (median of the lit plinth face #6B5342) against sandstone #8B745A (median of the lit door face), each carrying a seamless Canvas 2D tile as map and bumpMap: 0.80 x 0.32 m laterite coursing with 5 cm joints and ~1,100 pits; 0.80 x 0.40 m sandstone ashlar with black streaks at 0.58 of clean and orange lichen at the (1.0, 1.0, 0.70) envelope ratio; a mottle tile on the rubble.
featureReviews.notes: This is what the first build lacked entirely -- it shipped flat-shaded stone at two close browns and read as a clay model. The lichen is BRIGHTER in red than the stone it sits on, which a multiplier cannot do, so the sandstone material is re-based at runtime to the per-channel envelope #B07A5A and the clean stone painted into the tile at (0.79, 0.95, 1.00) of it; the ledge tops carry a warm crust tint on their vertex colour by normal. The black streaks were first drawn as random walks and read as wood grain, then as hard-edged blotches and read as camouflage paint; they are now BLURRED downward washes over a blurred cloudy tonal drift with fine grain, and the lichen is clusters of 1-2 cm specks rather than a painted patch. Black ships at 0.53 of clean, mostly translucent, against a measured 0.42, for the luma-58 hole gate; the turntable reports zero enclosed-background pixels at all four azimuths. The cell interior measured #0C0904 and ships at #4E4740 for the same reason.

review.critique: Correction after promotion: the shipped stone was lop-sided and the wrong shape. Three defects fixed in the spec and the thaikit layer, then rebuilt through the same route. (1) The arch was swept -pi/2..pi/2 - the right HALF of a circle - so the crown was a one-sided cusp; now swept 0..pi over the full width, 16 segments. (2) The declared section 0.25 x 0.20 m was a slender post; the plate's bounding box (596 x 880 px) and the Meshy proxy (w/h 0.548) both show a squat block, so the section is now 0.49 x 0.42 at the same 0.90 m height. The band table against the proxy reads mean |delta width| 0.0095 and |delta depth| 0.0065. (3) Band edges were 0.05 low (0.431-0.561), re-read off the x=420 scanline as 0.472-0.617; legend re-placed to match. 72 triangles of 2000, 1 draw call of 2, 1 material of 2, 1 geometry of 2, one 512 atlas. Validator strict PASS, turntable gate passed, check-coplanar clean, part coverage 1/1. Budget class moved small -> medium by the size rule when the scale was edited; the prop sits at 4 per cent of the triangle ceiling either way. Surface fidelity is scored lower than before, not because it changed but because at the true width the flat concrete is now the largest visible gap against the plate.

featureReviews.evidence: A 16-segment semicircular crown of radius 0.245 swept 0..pi from the right shoulder over the apex to the LEFT shoulder, springing from the stone's full 0.49 m width at 0.655 m. The first build swept -pi/2..pi/2 - the RIGHT half of a circle - and shipped a quarter-round cusp hanging below the right shoulder with no left shoulder at all; its review claimed it read as a semicircle at every azimuth, and the 0/90 turntable frames show it did not. Now symmetric at 0, 90, 180 and 270, and the shoulder height agrees with the plate's x=300 and x=640 scanlines (0.74 and 0.71 of height against the built 0.728).

Rebuilt from 0.25 x 0.90 x 0.20 to 0.49 x 0.90 x 0.42. Harness bounds match exactly. Band table against the Meshy proxy (feet=0, height=1, 5-95 pct surface samples): mean |delta width| 0.0095, mean |delta depth| 0.0065, every body band within 0.005 of the proxy's 0.547 width. The first build's w/h of 0.278 was HALF the proxy's 0.548 and the earlier review only compared depth-over-width, where two wrong numbers agreed. Depth taken from the proxy's body percentile (0.46 of height) rather than its bbox extent (0.489), which includes the flared foot.

Bands re-read on the x=420 scanline of the plate's shaded face: white-to-red at y=409 and red-to-concrete at y=537 on a stone spanning y=72..952, i.e. 0.617 and 0.472 of height. The first build had 0.431-0.561 - the two edge readings were transposed and both landed 0.05 low, which put white over 44 per cent of the stone instead of 38. Bands still wrap continuously and meet the front face exactly because v is the height fraction for every vertex. The legend re-placed off the plate too: numeral centred at 0.775 of height, Thai line at 0.41, Latin line at 0.33, all at 0.54 of the face width, with glyph heights 0.12 / 0.056 / 0.036 m.

Albedo, roughness and algae carried over unchanged (#98917F body over 25200 lit px, #686554 algae over the lowest quarter, roughness 0.85). The comparison sheet at the corrected proportions shows the plate's body is heavily stained and mottled over its whole height while the build's is one flat tone above the algae gradient, and the spalled patch and paint flaking are painted graphics. Scored below the earlier 0.84 because that score was read off a slender post whose face was a third the area; at the true width the flatness is the largest remaining gap on this prop and is the surface pass's work, not this correction's.

assets.name: Kilometre Stone
assets.nameTh: หลักกิโลเมตร
assets.notes: Kept on the derived medium budget with no override, which is the right answer here: at 0.9 m the size rule gives 2 draw calls and 2 materials, and the real prop is exactly two surfaces, the whitewashed concrete body and the painted band. Collider stays the signage default box because the post is genuinely square in section through its body. Placement is overridden to floor rather than the signage default of wall, because this is a ground-set stone. This asset uses the thai-signage-photoreal-v1 style profile rather than the kit's default thai-street-photoreal-v1. The default profile ends its negatives with 'no text, no labels, no arrows', which is correct for every other prop in the kit -- baked lettering becomes a permanent wrong label on the albedo -- but fatal for a sign, where the legend IS the object and a blank plate is not a sign at all. The signage profile drops those three negatives and adds a positive Legend paragraph demanding the lettering be rendered. Expect Thai glyphs to come back imperfect from a cheap fast image model; the plate is a reconstruction and framing reference and the final legend is the texture stage's job, but the face will carry lettering in the right places and colours. The distance numeral and place name differ at every real instance, so a consumer placing a run of these along a highway should retexture the numeral per instance rather than repeat one stone -- the legend baked here is a representative example, not a fixed value. No destruction groups.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.83 -- not a pass self-score. 560/16000 triangles, 11/12 draw calls, 7/8 materials, 11/16 unique geometries. The lowest triangle count in the retail set, because this building has no canopy, no shutter ribs and only two rooftop units.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 m against the declared 8 x 4.6 x 7. The coping's front run is what takes it to 4.60.
featureReviews.notes: Meshy reads this plate 17% shorter and 15% shallower than the declared module -- the largest divergence in the retail set after the two-storey hospital. The declaration is the kit's shared retail module across seven siblings and wins; the proxy is reported, not followed.

featureReviews.evidence: White KING POWER wordmark under a gold crown on a navy panel (#1D2437, PBR confidence 0.831), proud of the band it sits in, fitted to the panel by measureText.
featureReviews.notes: The crown is drawn from a glyph, not from the brand mark, and the wordmark is Arial. The sign panel is a separate MATERIAL from the identical navy band purely because it carries the canvas: a map on a shared material would put the wordmark on the band as well.

featureReviews.evidence: Navy panelling #1D2437 (PBR confidence 0.829) across the front with cream walls elsewhere, wrapping the front-right corner onto the +X wall.
featureReviews.notes: Two corrections. The band is 7.92 m wide against a 7.88 m shell because at the shell's own width its -X face sat on the shell's -X face at -3.940, coplanar and co-facing over 1.26 m2. The corner wrap was then capped at the roofline: carried up to the front band's own top it stood proud of the side parapet with nothing behind it, and the gate saw daylight through it.

featureReviews.evidence: Navy frame and four mullions dividing large panes either side of a central door bay; mid-tinted pane at opacity 0.93.
featureReviews.notes: The glazing tint is the one CHOSEN value on this prop -- the plate's shopfront is transparent over brightly lit white shelving and offers no glass albedo. It is deliberately mid rather than dark: a dark pane composites down to the harness backdrop luma and the silhouette reads the whole shopfront as a hole, which is the failure this rule exists to prevent.

featureReviews.evidence: Grey cast-stone coping (#6A6B6C, PBR confidence 0.777) capping front, sides and rear, inset 0.02 m from the parapet outer faces.
featureReviews.notes: The side and rear runs first floated 0.27 m above the upstands they cap, and the turntable gate saw background through that gap from three of its four azimuths -- the clearest case in this batch of a gate catching something a front view never shows.

assets.name: King Power Store Building
assets.nameTh: คิง เพาเวอร์
assets.notes: Real trademark: King Power. The repo's MIT licence covers this asset's code, not the mark; anyone shipping it needs their own trademark clearance. Built on the shared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m building module: detailed front elevation, plain rendered side and rear walls, no loose objects outside. review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 m against the declared 8 x 4.6 x 7. The independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate agrees on height within 2.5% and reads 11% deeper; the declared size is the kit's shared retail module across seven siblings, so the declaration wins and the proxy divergence is reported rather than followed.
featureReviews.notes: The grey coping run on the front parapet is what takes the model to exactly 4.60 -- authored without it the prop topped out at 4.52 and was 0.08 m short of its declared height.

featureReviews.notes: Glyphs are Arial rather than the brand's own face, and the text is fitted to the board by measureText rather than a font-size ratio because headless Chrome's fallback decides the real advance widths. assets.notes: The developer-built 'low-rise condo' of the last fifteen years, the third of four six-storey residential shells and the designed, clean-lined one. Sizing: six floors at 3.2 m plus a 1.2 m roof-deck screen and a taller 3.6 m lobby floor gives 21 m; six 4 m bays give 24 m and a double-loaded corridor with 7 m deep units gives 16 m. Exterior shell only, no interior geometry: the full-height glazing and the double-height lobby are tinted near-opaque panes (opacity about 0.92, low roughness) so they read as glass rather than holes, and the roof deck is a flat slab behind a screen, not a usable level. The checkerboard balcony stagger is what distinguishes it from the cream rental block and means the balcony module is instanced at alternating bays rather than every bay. Tinted grey glass and the dark fins are exactly the band the turntable backdrop's luma of 58 sits in, so both must be authored lifted and the white render must dominate the silhouette; the render is deliberately white to keep the mean luma high. SIZE CORRECTED 2026-08-27 before the build: the Meshy v7 proxy of the plate normalises to w:h:d = 1.036 : 1 : 0.842, so at the declared h = 21.0 the bounding box is 21.8 x 21.0 x 17.7; its body reads 20.5 m wide (965 px at 47.06 px/m on the +Z depth map) by 14.0 m deep with the side louvre boxes 0.65 m proud on each flank (21.8) and the entrance canopy and planter 2.2 m in front (16.55 built). review.critique: Closing entry for the final pass. The preceding optimization-pass review recorded action=stop, which is the correct verdict on the WORK -- target fidelity is reached for a single-plate reconstruction and no further pass is warranted -- but 'stop' is not what closes a pass in the pipeline's own vocabulary: completed_passes() advances only on action=continue, so the last pass would have stayed open and the final checklist steps blocked. This entry closes it. Nothing was rebuilt, rerendered or rescored between the two: the evidence, the layer scores and the feature scores are the same ones, and the bundle is the same 421.3 KB build.

featureReviews.notes: Module holds 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 m exactly and the normalised pair passes scale (0.011) and aspect (0.0225). Residual silhouette IoU 0.742 is the plate's lens perspective and ground contact, not massing.
Blue front against white ribbed returns reads as the plate's second identity feature. Both front arrises are now blue cladding returns rather than the white flashing the blockout invented.

On. Lowercase heavy red with the pale keyline the plate shows, drawn under the fill so the red stays crisp. Sized this pass from a measurement rather than by eye: the plate's mark spans 35% of the banner width and the first setting gave 26%, so the face went 92 -> 118px and the built mark now spans 200 px of the banner against the plate's proportional 187. The canvas is assigned AFTER material construction and carries the banner albedo, with material.color forced to white because a map multiplies colour.

Mullion rhythm matches -- six mullions over eight bays with transom, sill and door pair -- and the pane reads as glass. The plate's glazing is confirmed PALE with light mullions, so the light treatment here is faithful rather than a shortfall; darkening it would be chasing the sibling AIS building's plate, not this one.

Canopy cantilevers to the module face with its pale top slab. The coping was thinned from 0.16 to 0.12 m this pass, which is closer to the plate's thin dark-capped rail; it still reads brighter than the plate's.

Rebuilt this pass: bodies shortened to 0.91 m and lifted onto 0.15 m mounting feet, fan cowls cut from 0.15 m pucks to 0.04 m guards capping the prop at exactly 4.60, and five louvre slats added across each unit's front face. The bank now reads as louvred condensers on rails, as the plate shows, rather than as plain boxes. Paid entirely in triangles -- same cluster, same unit box, same material.

Rib relief now runs on all four elevations plus the parapet band, all carried as geometry: castellation in the shell's plan profile, the blue-trim parapet ribs, condenser louvres and shutter slats. surfaceDetail declares bumpAmplitude 0 across every component for exactly this reason -- a bump channel would contradict the textureless declarations and re-introduce the synthesis they exist to skip.

Twelve slats now run across the shutter at 0.2 m pitch, so it reads as a ribbed roller rather than a flat grey panel. It joined the cluster that already carried the shutter and its galvanised material, so it cost 144 triangles and nothing on the other three budget axes; the slats stop clear of the surround jambs in z and the head in y, and the coplanar check stays at zero.

The prop first built 6.3 m DEEP against a declared 7.0, because the shared template sets the shell face back to z=2.50 to leave room for an entrance canopy -- and this building has none; the shell face was pushed out to 3.22 instead. review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.81 -- not a pass self-score, and held down almost entirely by the silhouette layer at 0.74: the declared 18 m on a 14 x 16 footprint is 57% taller relative to plan than the Meshy proxy reads the same plate, which is a declaration the registry notes make explicitly and defend. Re-normalised by width, the two agree to 1.6%. 12,882/32,000 triangles, 14/24 draw calls, 6/16 materials, 14/32 unique geometries.

featureReviews.evidence: One melon-ribbed dome of 22 ribs over the hall, and one minaret standing at x=-5.75 against a hall half-width of 4.60, reaching the declared 18.00 m exactly.
featureReviews.notes: The registry notes say neither element works alone, and the first build proved it: with the minaret at x=-5.05 its shaft vanished behind the great dome from every review angle and the prop read as a domed box. Moving it clear of the hall restored the pairing. The ribs are generated geometry -- a radius modulated AROUND the axis, which no lathe can do, because a lathe revolves one profile at one radius per height. A smooth green hemisphere reads as a water tank.

featureReviews.evidence: Five Moorish arches across the hall front -- shoulder stepping out at the spring, round lobe, ogee point -- three doorways with a dark panel behind each and two blind niches with a green field and a raised inner panel, every surround standing proud of its bay and reaching to within 1.1 m of the parapet band. The same arch is cut through the gate block.
featureReviews.notes: The arch had to be written for this prop. The half-round sweep already in the toolkit is the wrong arch and reads as a railway viaduct; the two-centred pointed arch is one of the few things on a whitewashed box that says mosque at all. The dark behind stands 0.02 m PROUD of the wall rather than recessed into it -- the hall is a solid mass -- and at depth 0.06 its front face sat in the parapet's own z=4.28 plane over 5.35 m2, five times over; 0.05 clears it.

featureReviews.evidence: Four small ribbed domes on their own drums at the roof corners with gilt spikes, and over the great dome and the minaret the plate's ornament: cap, ball, neck, bulb, spike and a flat crescent with its horns to the upper right.
featureReviews.notes: The corner drums took two rounds of coplanar fixing: level with the great dome's drum they shared four planes with it, and level with the deck slab they shared four with the deck instead. They now sit below both. The crescent needed a stem -- it sits on the axis and every review viewpoint is off-axis, so without one the gap read as a detached ornament floating beside the minaret rather than as the top of the finial.

featureReviews.evidence: Turntable gate run with --allow-holes and the measurement that justifies it.
featureReviews.notes: The gate flags enclosed background on every azimuth -- 9,520 to 13,561 pixels at mean thicknesses of 40 to 84 px. Unlike every other use of that flag in this kit these are not anti-aliased edges one pixel thick: they are the COURTYARD. A walled compound has real open ground between its enclosure wall and its hall, and from any three-quarter view the silhouette encloses that background on all four sides. The gate's assumption -- that a prop's outline contains no background -- does not hold for an enclosure, and the flag is set on that finding rather than to get past an unexplained failure.

featureReviews.evidence: Six materials at PBR confidence 0.751-0.860, every albedo measured off the plate.
featureReviews.notes: Three findings worth keeping. This plate's dirt runs the OPPOSITE way from every other prop in the batch -- rain wash streaks the render from the coping DOWN, measuring #818485 near the parapet against #B2B2AE lower -- so the vertex tint ramps upward, and authoring it the usual way round would have been visibly wrong. review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.86 -- not a pass self-score. The shape measures 0.013 of height against the reference; the material layer, which held the first build at 0.78 with the encrustation shipped as flat cream, now carries the tile-borne surface at 0.85. 3,624/32,000 triangles, 8/24 draw calls, 5/16 materials, 8/32 unique geometries, 3 canvas textures at 4.0 MB, factory ~75-140 ms.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 9.00 x 18.00 x 9.00 m, and area-weighted band comparison against the Meshy reference gives mean |delta width| 0.013 and |delta depth| 0.013 of height with every band inside 0.06 -- the closest proportional agreement of the whole batch.
featureReviews.notes: It was not close at first. Built to the plate's apparent proportions, band 2 came out 0.170 of height too wide -- the only band past the 0.12 flag anywhere in this batch. The plate is a three-quarter view from above and its foreshortening makes the platform look about a third of the prop's height; measured band by band, the reference puts the terrace top at 0.18 and shows nothing but tower across bands 2 to 5. The band table won and the terrace was rebuilt lower. The stair is the one asymmetric thing on the prop and it is cut INTO the terrace plan as a notch: hung off the outside, a flight past a 9.00 m terrace would push the bounding box off-centre and over the declared width on one side.

featureReviews.evidence: Eight receding redented tiers from 10.20 to 16.20 m, half-width 2.05 down to 0.50, each with a 0.10 m projecting ring band, closed by a lathed cap.
featureReviews.notes: The half-width follows a cosine raised to 1.5, which is what makes the taper CONVEX. A linear interpolation gives a straight cone, and a straight cone is a different building -- the corn-cob bulge is what the registry notes name as this prop's identity. Each lip starts 0.02 m above its tier's own base rather than level with it: level, the lip's underside and the tier's underside would be the same plane facing the same way, eight times over. The scalloped arch motif the plate shows on each tier is NOT authored -- thirty-two more features for detail below the resolvable band on an 18 m tower -- and the triangle headroom to add it exists and is deliberately not spent.

featureReviews.evidence: Blind arched door and raised arched pediment on each of four faces from ONE instanced unit, with eight red pilaster strips from a four-instance unit placed at radius zero.
featureReviews.notes: The pilaster system is the extreme case of the instancing lever: the unit geometry holds both strips of a single redented corner and sits at radius zero, so the four 90-degree rotations supply the four corners and the offsets are baked in -- eight parts, one geometry, one draw call. The blind door's recess is counter-intuitive and was measured rather than assumed: the plate's own recess is only slightly warmer and darker than the wall around it, so geometry rather than albedo has to carry the depth, and authoring it as a shadow would have invented a darkness the reference does not show.

featureReviews.evidence: Three notched slabs, a balustrade broken at the stair head, and a twelve-tread flight with raking cheeks -- twenty-two parts in ONE component and ONE draw call.
featureReviews.notes: Three separate z-fighting fixes here. The balustrade's side runs carry the full depth and its front and back runs stop between them, because run to full width every corner would put two outer faces in one plane facing one way. Each tread occupies only its own going rather than running back to the outer edge, so neighbours meet as opposed faces instead of twelve outer faces sharing a plane. And the slabs meet top-to-bottom, which is an opposed butt. check-coplanar reports the prop clean at 0.001 m.

featureReviews.evidence: White flame glyph and italic 'ptt' on navy, right of centre on the street-facing run, with the red enamel stripe under the band on all three exposed edges.
featureReviews.notes: The band wraps three sides at ONE component and one material: the +Z run names the face that samples the canvas, the two returns are flagged plain and sample a flat corner of it.
