review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.79, the lowest of the fifteen and honestly so -- held down by the silhouette layer at 0.72, which has NO reference mesh behind it. Meshy refused this plate with content_policy_violation, so this is the only prop in the batch whose proportions were never checked band by band, and that check caught the largest errors on three of the other props. 2,308/32,000 triangles, 8/24 draw calls, 5/16 materials, 8/32 unique geometries.

featureReviews.evidence: A 22.5 m figure on its RIGHT side facing the colonnade, head at +Z: one smooth body from neck to ankle, taller than deep, the upper leg a soft ridge on it, stacked feet with a toe comb, an upright tilted head with ushnisha and ear lobes cupped in the right hand, the forearm near-vertical from an elbow on the plinth, the left arm along the flank to a hand on the thigh.
featureReviews.notes: The only organic form in the kit, and it needed a shape helper written for it alone: a reclining body is a long soft mass whose section changes at every point along it, and a box decomposition of that is not a low-poly body but a pile of luggage. Every station's centre height is DERIVED from its own radius -- cy = plinth top + ry, computed rather than authored -- which is the only way a varying section can rest on a flat plinth at every point. The first promoted build was ONE symmetric tube from head to feet with the head at -Z, and it read as a figure on its back facing the wall; the rebuild carries the asymmetry that says on-its-side. Two earlier pose faults were found by review rather than by a gate: the arm ran too high and too far and covered the head entirely from the +X side, which is the only side anyone sees this prop from, and the ushnisha wanted 0.70 m of height where the soffit leaves 0.50.

featureReviews.evidence: Twelve columns leaving the whole long front open, with the figure legible through them along its length and a dark interior face at luma 82 behind.
featureReviews.notes: The registry notes require this and give the reason: a closed long low box has no recognisable feature at all and reads as a warehouse. The interior shade fills the gaps between twelve columns, so its luma margin over the backdrop's 58 matters more here than anywhere -- at the backdrop value the gate would read eleven separate holes through the building. Its two panels also had to drop from 6.60 to 6.54: at the column head height each shared that plane with every column, and because the columns are an InstancedMesh, check-coplanar reported one mistake as twelve pairs.

featureReviews.evidence: Two tiers at pitch 0.64 -- about 33 degrees -- from eaves at 6.60 to a ridge at 9.78, with a gold border along both eaves and bargeboards lying on every rake.
featureReviews.notes: The pitch is deliberately NOT the ubosot's 46 degrees: this is a long low hall and a steep roof would have made a different building. That shallower pitch also exposed a real bug carried over from the ubosot. The rake angle is atan2(RUN, RISE), not atan(pitch) -- rotateZ maps a box's +Y to (-sin, cos), so aiming it along the rake needs the COMPLEMENT of the pitch angle. At 46 degrees the two are three degrees apart and the error is invisible; at 33 they are twenty-four apart and the boards stood off the roof like scaffolding. Fixed in both props. The roof is also centred at x=-1.72 rather than on the origin, because the hall sits at one side of the platform and the forward apron takes the rest.

featureReviews.evidence: Five materials at PBR confidence 0.822-0.860, four measured on lit faces and the fifth corrected with its reasoning recorded.
featureReviews.notes: The gilt is the largest deliberate deviation on the prop. The figure is the ONE surface in this plate that is never directly lit -- deep shade, behind columns, under a soffit -- so its mean across 41,296 warm-hued pixels, #7D6040, is illumination and not albedo, and renders the figure brown. The albedo taken is the brightest QUARTILE of those pixels, #AC8E6F, which is the same 'measure a lit face' rule applied to a surface that has no lit face; the brightest 8% at #BEA07E was tried first and rendered cream. It ships at #AC7741: that hue and value kept exactly, chroma raised from 0.36 to 0.62, with metalness halved to 0.15 because a metal with no environment map has its diffuse scaled by (1-metalness) and drains the chroma out of exactly the surface that has to read as gold.

assets.name: Road Crossroads Tile
assets.nameTh: ถนนสี่แยก
assets.notes: One flat quad, 8 x 8 m, lying in the ground plane at y=0 -- two triangles, one geometry, one draw call, one PBR material, and nothing else. The entire street reads out of the texture: carriageway, lane markings, kerb line, sidewalk slabs, drain grates and manhole covers are painted into the maps, never built. The earlier procedural version of this tile modelled a raised 0.15 m kerb and sidewalk and it did not work, so the flat quad replaces it outright -- there is no kerb to step up onto and a player walks the sidewalk band at road level. Budget overridden explicitly to 2 triangles / 1 draw call / 1 material / 1 unique geometry instead of the hero2x its 8 m footprint would derive: footprint drives the class, but there is no geometry here to spend a class budget on. Quality comes entirely from a high-end PBR texture generator -- albedo, roughness, normal and AO at photoreal fidelity matched to the reference plate -- and not from mesh detail; that is the whole bet of this piece. Fit is the one hard requirement: the footprint is exactly 8 x 8 m on the kit's 8 m grid, which is also the frontage of the kit's shop buildings so a tile row lines up with a shophouse row; the pivot is base-center so tiles snap on 8 m centres; and every road-facing edge carries the same band profile -- 1.25 m sidewalk, 5.5 m two-lane carriageway, 1.25 m sidewalk. Any tile edge must therefore meet any other, and the texture has to be edge-matched to the rest of the set at those band boundaries: asphalt tone, kerb-line position and sidewalk slab coursing must continue across a seam without a visible join. No destruction groups: a road tile is static level geometry, not a breakable. Rotationally symmetric on all four edges, so it can be dropped in at any of four orientations, which makes it the piece that closes a street grid -- and that symmetry is a constraint on the texture, not just a property of it: the four band profiles must be identical to the pixel at the tile boundary or one of the four rotations will show a seam the other three do not. The open centre carries no lane markings at all because real junctions wear them away, which also keeps the centre from having to agree with whatever meets it on each approach.

assets.name: Robot-Face Stepped Office Tower
assets.nameTh: ตึกหุ่นยนต์
assets.notes: The shortest and squarest of the fifteen imposters, a 1980s postmodern office block; it sits in the mid-distance rather than on the horizon. Aspect 2:3 keeps the full stepped outline with margin. Skyline imposter, not a building model: the deliverable is ONE upright quad (2 triangles, 1 draw call, 1 material, 1 geometry) carrying this asset's plate as its texture with the flat grey backdrop keyed to alpha, placed 150-300 m out beyond the playable area and yawed each frame to face the camera. No Meshy reference mesh and no img2threejs sculpt: the plate IS the model. budgetClass is overridden to small because that is exactly the quad's budget; the size-derived hero8x would ask for 64k triangles and 48 draw calls nobody needs. collider none because nothing in play can reach it. Depth is declared 0.1 m because a quad has none and the schema wants a positive number; width and height are the real building's so the quad is placed at true scale. Plate: style profile thai-skyline-imposter-v1 (straight-on telephoto elevation, whole building, flat grey where sky and ground would be), generated with fal-ai/nano-banana-2 at resolution 2K in aspect_ratio 2:3, chosen as the narrowest supported ratio still wider than the declared w:h. The RAW 2K output is the texture and must be kept beside the asset; assets/<id>/preview.jpg is the 1024-square registry plate only. Forms are generic Bangkok archetypes, not any named landmark or brand. Width corrected from the plate on 2026-08-27: keyed silhouette aspect 0.443 x declared height 83 m = 36.8 m against the listed 50 m (26% off); the quad carries the plate at true height so its width must follow the plate or the texture stretches.

The RAW 2K output is the texture and must be kept beside the asset; assets/<id>/preview.jpg is the 1024-square registry plate only. Forms are generic Bangkok archetypes, not any named landmark or brand. assets.notes: A flat 8 x 8 m street quad with a numbered soi entrance sign standing on it: two triangles for the deck plus a post and a board, so three draw calls, three unique geometries and three materials. Every other tile in the set is a bare quad; this one is the exception, and it is deliberate -- the sign is what tells a player this gap between buildings is a named soi rather than a service alley, and a level builder should not have to remember to stand a separate prop on the right corner of the right tile. The street itself still reads entirely out of the texture: paving, drain lids, edge strips, markings and covers are painted into the maps, never built. There is no kerb to step up onto and no recess in the drain -- the drain reads as a channel because of its albedo, normal and AO, not because there is a hole there. Budget overridden explicitly to 200 triangles / 3 draw calls / 3 materials / 3 unique geometries instead of the hero2x its 8 m footprint would derive: footprint drives the class, but the only geometry here is the sign. Quality of the ground comes entirely from a high-end PBR texture generator -- albedo, roughness, normal and AO at photoreal fidelity matched to the reference plate -- and not from mesh detail. Fit is the one hard requirement. The footprint is exactly 8 x 8 m on the kit's 8 m grid, which is also the frontage of the kit's shop buildings so a tile row lines up with a shophouse row. The pivot is base-center. This is the adapter of the kit and the only piece carrying two different edge profiles: three edges are the standard road profile of 1.25 m sidewalk band, 5.5 m two-lane carriageway and 1.25 m sidewalk band, and the fourth is the alley profile of a 0.5 m edge band, a 3 m paved alley and a 0.5 m edge band. Without this piece the alley tiles connect to nothing, so its two profiles must be edge-matched in two directions at once -- against the road set on three edges and against the alley set on the fourth. The alley mouth sits at 4.5 to 7.5 m along its south edge, which is exactly 0.5 to 3.5 m within the 4 m alley tile that mates against the eastern half-module; that offset is part of the contract, because a soi is a gap between buildings rather than a designed junction. The texture has to be edge-matched to the rest of the set at those band boundaries: surface tone, edge-strip position, drain-lid coursing and slab joints must continue across a seam without a visible join. The sidewalk ramp across the mouth is paint and texture rather than geometry, which costs nothing here because the kerb it used to ramp down from is gone. No destruction groups: a road tile is static level geometry, not a breakable, and the sign does not come off. The sign has no moving parts either, so the whole piece ships one root pivot and no sockets.

review.critique: Two-component street-name sign built to the declared 0.750 x 2.200 m with a measured depth inside the asset's 0.1 tolerance. 452 triangles of 800, 2 draw calls of 2, 2 materials of 2, 2 unique geometries of 2, one texture. The passes were worked as ONE build with the deterministic gates run once over the finished prop rather than per pass; the per-pass content is real but the per-pass evidence is not, and that is stated rather than implied. Two measurements here contradict the sibling signs built in the same session and both were kept: the field is a DEEP navy #2B4278 against the informatory plates' #3370AB and #4871A2, and the folded edge return is PAINTED navy #55678D rather than the bare metal grey every sibling shows. Assuming either from a sibling would have put a metal band round a painted plate and lit the wrong blue behind the legend.

featureReviews.evidence: A 20-point rounded-rect extrusion at 0.75 x 0.22 m with a 12 mm radius - the shallowest plate in the set at a 3.41 aspect, where every sibling is portrait or square. Edge-on it reads as a 35 mm folded pressing. Held at 0.88 because a landscape plate this thin is the hardest of the eight to read off a three-quarter view and its height is the least certain number in the spec.

Graded against the DECLARED contract: 0.75 x 2.20 m built exactly, plate occupying 0.10 of total height, matching the Meshy proxy's own plate band extent of 0.3 scaled to the declared plate height. Tube diameter 48 mm from the proxy's normalised shaft width of 0.049.

A CylinderGeometry at 12 radial segments, not the BoxGeometry every other support in this set uses. This is the prop's one structural difference from its siblings and the reference is unambiguous: a continuous curved highlight runs the length of the shaft with no arris anywhere. The collider proxy is EXACT here rather than circumscribing, because the support really is a round tube. 288 of the prop's 452 triangles are in this component - the only prop in the set where the support outweighs the plate, and deliberate, because a round section read as a polygon is the one defect a viewer notices on a tube.

Border rule, Thai soi name, Latin transliteration and the soi number at the right end all ride one UV atlas on one material. The arrangement is asymmetric - the number sits right - and the front-cap UV mapping preserves the sign so the atlas is not mirrored. The legend is representative text, not a transcription of the reference's particular soi: this is a kit prop, not a copy of one street's sign.

Ramp baked as vertex colours over 12 height segments, no texture. This is the only support in the set given a RAMP rather than a hard splash line, and the reason is measured: 2586 of 4500 px in the foot crop pass the orange filter against 584 of 4050 on the u-turn post, so this tube is corroding through rather than carrying a splash stain and a hard edge would be the wrong shape for it.

review.critique: Two-component sign built to the declared 0.600 x 2.300 x 0.080 m, measured by the harness, not estimated. 444 triangles of 800, 2 draw calls of 2, 2 materials of 2, 2 unique geometries of 2, one texture, createObjectModel returning in 37 ms. The passes were worked as ONE build with the deterministic gates run once over the finished prop rather than per pass, so this entry records the same evidence set for each pass: the per-pass content is real but the per-pass evidence is not, and that is stated rather than implied. Two corrections were taken and both are recorded. First, the spangle noise was re-keyed from vertex INDEX to quantised POSITION - on a non-indexed buffer an index key gives the three corners of every triangle different values, and the post rendered as a patchwork of flat facets. Second, the rust ramp was re-measured after the first version faded rust in from 1.5 m in a desaturated grey-brown, an artefact of trimming a crop that held both rust and clean coating; splitting the two populations by hue put the rust at #6E5641 confined below 0.30 m with a hard splash line.

featureReviews.evidence: 72 radial segments. The rim reads as a true circle at every azimuth in the 8-frame turntable, and edge-on at 90/270 it reads as a thin plate rather than a wedge. 288 of the prop's 444 triangles are here, which is the only place they were spent.

Graded against the DECLARED registry contract, which is this prop's target, and not against the plate. The harness measured the built bounds at 0.600 x 2.300 x 0.080 m against a declared 0.6 x 2.3 x 0.08 - exact on all three axes, with the flange foot setting the depth exactly as the Meshy proxy's band scan predicted (its lowest band is its deepest, 0.073 of height against the disc bands' 0.008 to 0.041). Disc centre at 1.98 m is a real regulatory mounting height. THE PLATE DISAGREES AND IS NOT BEING MATCHED: the plate and its Meshy proxy both render the disc at 0.44-0.45 of total height (a ~1.0 m disc), which is not a real regulatory proportion for a 0.6 m sign. A reviewer comparing render to plate will see a visibly smaller disc; that is the intended result, is recorded in assumptions and risks, and is the reason this feature is graded against the contract rather than against the image.

Rim band 1.00R-0.95R, red annulus 0.95R-0.717R and cream ground inside it, all taken off the x=515 scanline rather than estimated; numerals at the plate's measured 1.13R width; two bolt heads at 0.74R. All four ride one UV atlas on one material, so the printed front and the bare aluminium back cost one draw call between them - confirmed in the 180 render, which shows a plain grey disc.

CORRECTED during the build. The first ramp faded rust in from 1.5 m at #7D6C5F, both wrong, because the crop trimmed to produce it contained rust AND clean coating. Separating the populations by hue gives rust #6E5641/#72553E confined below 0.30 m, with a per-band orange-pixel count reading 0 percent from 0.44 m to 1.08 m and 56 percent at 0.23 m. Shaft raised to 16 height segments so the splash line lands on a segment boundary and resolves as an edge. Held short of 0.9 because the plate's heavy white spangle STREAKING is not reproduced - the vertex ramp carries the vertical trend and a low-amplitude blotch, not the streaks.

Shaft runs 0.018 m to 2.28 m, past the back of the disc, capped by a 0.02 m bracket to 2.30 m and landing on a 0.16 x 0.018 x 0.08 m flange. Visible in the 180 render. The cap peeks only ~20 mm above the disc's top edge where the plate shows a more prominent bracket.

review.critique: Two-component twin-post directional sign built to the declared 1.200 x 2.400 m. 580 triangles of 800, 2 draw calls of 2, 2 materials of 3, 2 unique geometries of 3, one texture. The passes were worked as ONE build with the deterministic gates run once over the finished prop rather than per pass; the per-pass content is real but the per-pass evidence is not, and that is stated rather than implied. Two splits were refused and both are recorded where someone tempted to make them will read them: the two legs are merged into ONE buffer rather than given a component each, which is the whole reason this prop fits two draw calls; and the wide painted frame is a printed region of the board's face rather than a modelled solid. The third material and third geometry were both available and neither was spent.

featureReviews.evidence: A 20-point rounded-rect extrusion at 1.2 x 0.62 m with a 12 mm radius - near-square corners, because the reference shows a framed board with sharp mitred corners rather than the design radii the informatory plates carry. Held at 0.86 because the board height is the lowest-confidence dimension in the spec: it comes from the Meshy proxy's band extent scaled against the declared width, not from a measurement of the image.

Two 48 mm round tubes at x = -0.405 and +0.405, merged into ONE BufferGeometry. Built as a genuine REFLECTION - the lateral axis negated and nothing else - rather than by rotating, so the chirality rule holds even though both tubes are surfaces of revolution and the distinction cannot show here. 440 of the prop's 580 triangles are in this component, which is right: a round section read as a polygon is the one defect a viewer notices on a tube, and there are two of them.

Wide painted frame, Thai place name, Latin transliteration and the direction arrow all ride ONE atlas on ONE material along with the weathered back. The arrow points RIGHT and that is chiral - an arrow the other way sends traffic the wrong way - and the front-cap UV mapping preserves the sign so the atlas is not mirrored.

Roughness 0.72 and materialClass wood, matte where every sibling in this set is satin vinyl at 0.42 - this is the only prop of the eight whose panel is painted timber, and treating it as sheeting would have been the easy error. Brown #655851 is a warm NEUTRAL rather than a printed colour, measured over 7200 px. Held at 0.78 because the paint flaking off the frame's arrises is drawn as scattered rectangles, which reads correctly at prop distance but is graphic rather than organic at close range.

Ramp baked as vertex colours over 10 height segments per tube, no texture, shared across both legs because the reference weathers them identically. The clean value rests on 7497 of 7500 neutral pixels - the cleanest galvanising reading of the eight props, against the no-parking post's 186. A RAMP rather than a hard splash line, because the reference shows rust climbing both tubes over their lower third with no top edge.

assets.name: Twin Office Towers with Sky Bridge
assets.nameTh: ตึกแฝดสะพานลอยฟ้า
assets.notes: One imposter, two towers: they share one quad on purpose because the sky bridge joins them, and splitting them would need two billboards that yaw apart. Declared width is the pair with the podium. Skyline imposter, not a building model: the deliverable is ONE upright quad (2 triangles, 1 draw call, 1 material, 1 geometry) carrying this asset's plate as its texture with the flat grey backdrop keyed to alpha, placed 150-300 m out beyond the playable area and yawed each frame to face the camera. No Meshy reference mesh and no img2threejs sculpt: the plate IS the model. budgetClass is overridden to small because that is exactly the quad's budget; the size-derived hero8x would ask for 64k triangles and 48 draw calls nobody needs. collider none because nothing in play can reach it. Depth is declared 0.1 m because a quad has none and the schema wants a positive number; width and height are the real building's so the quad is placed at true scale. Plate: style profile thai-skyline-imposter-v1 (straight-on telephoto elevation, whole building, flat grey where sky and ground would be), generated with fal-ai/nano-banana-2 at resolution 2K in aspect_ratio 2:3, chosen as the narrowest supported ratio still wider than the declared w:h. The RAW 2K output is the texture and must be kept beside the asset; assets/<id>/preview.jpg is the 1024-square registry plate only. Forms are generic Bangkok archetypes, not any named landmark or brand.

First, the plate's blue was re-measured after the first crop at (560,240,50,70) returned #869DB6: it overlapped the arrow's white right stroke, and a crop that holds two populations reports a colour on neither. Second, the plate was being offset TWICE - the generator applies the component transform to the parent node, and the layer was setting the mesh position as well, which floated the plate clear of the post.

featureReviews.evidence: A 20-point rounded-rect extrusion, four segments per corner, bevelEnabled:false so ExtrudeGeometry does not round the radius a second time. The corner radius is the only curve this plate has and it reads at every turntable azimuth; edge-on the plate reads as a 30 mm folded section rather than a wedge.

Graded against the DECLARED contract, which is the target. Harness-measured bounds 0.900 x 2.400 x 0.087 m against a declared 0.9 x 2.4 x 0.08 - exact in width and height, and inside tolerance in depth. Plate height 1.2 m is taken from the Meshy proxy's own band extent (bands 0.5-1.0 of total height), not estimated. The proxy's normalised width implies a 0.62 plate aspect against the 0.75 built from the declared 0.9 m width; the declared contract wins and the difference is recorded rather than matched.

Border rule, hooked arrow and both legend lines ride one UV atlas on one material, so the printed front and the bare edge return cost one draw call between them. The arrow is CHIRAL - it hooks one way - and the front-cap UV mapping preserves the sign so it is not mirrored; the render hooks the same way as the plate. Field #4871A2, legend #C3C4C2, edge #707272, each from its own filtered crop.

Ramp baked as vertex colours over 12 height segments, no texture. Rust #756353 from 584 orange-biased px, held below 0.26 m with a hard splash line because the per-band rusty-pixel scan reads 0 per cent at every band from y=600 to y=860 and 17-22 per cent below. Held short of 0.9 because the reference's post carries more surface mottle than a 12-segment vertex ramp can express.

featureReviews.notes: The first build was declared 12 m tall on a 24 m hall and read as a lid on a box; the proxy of the same plate normalises to long:h:short = 1 : 0.709 : 0.573 and the registry was re-declared to 14 x 17 x 24 for this rebuild. Every register height is read off the proxy's orthographic elevations (front.mjs side and end, occupancy map): skirt eaves hw 6.8 at 6.9 m, middle eaves hw 5.0 at 9.0 m, top eaves hw 3.1 at 10.9 m, ridges 14.8 m and 14.0 m, apex chofa to 17.0 m. The one band still over 0.05 is band 4 (6.8-8.5 m): the proxy's skirt fascia is taller than the 0.4 m built. Raising the skirt by 0.5 m halved that residual; the rest is the fascia's own height and is reported rather than chased.

featureReviews.evidence: A hipped 37-degree portico skirt, a 45-degree middle layer the full 18 m, and a top gable telescoped into a 12 m centre at 14.8 m and two 3 m ends at 14.0 m, each register a white riser, a glaze band and a tile field; white bargeboards with red strips; sixteen curved horns; one carved pediment per end gable.
featureReviews.notes: The first build nested three same-length tiers concentrically -- a wedding cake, not a Thai roof -- which is the structure the user returned. The proxy's side elevation shows the layer lines continuous along the length with only the ridges stepping, and its end elevation shows one gable triangle from the middle eaves to the ridge, so the end sections' top pitch is the middle layer's 45 degrees continued and the top layer's step shows only on the side slopes. The centre section's gable faces at z = +-6 show 0.8 m above the end ridges, which is the telescoped step the plate shows behind the near pediment. The skirt is quad-strip rings because it hips round the ends and no extrusion can do that; it closes with a soffit and an inner wall so the turntable gate cannot read through it.

featureReviews.evidence: Thirty red columns in a regular peristyle at ONE draw call under a red eaves beam, a parapet between their bases, sixteen windows and two doors in stone surrounds on the body, and eight bai sema on the bottom terrace with one centred before each stair.
featureReviews.notes: Counted off the plate's right-hand elevation: eleven a side and four between the corners on each end, against the first build's nine and three. The body was bare in the first build; the plate shows dark leaves in white surrounds between every column, and they are two instanced systems rather than thirty-two meshes. featureReviews.evidence: Seven materials at PBR confidence 0.735-0.860, every albedo measured off the plate, and four seamless Canvas 2D weathering tiles bound post-construction: streaked whitewash, peeling lacquer, laid tile courses with moss, and a carved gilt pediment. 4 textures, 5.3 MB, 68 ms.
featureReviews.notes: The user's brief was 'add a weathered texture on the outside' and the plate agrees: the whitewash is streaked grey-black and grimed at the plinth (600..700, 850..878 measures #828282 against the clean #BDA69A), the columns peel to pale plaster (p90 #C8A58C), the roof is laid in visible courses with grey-green growth. Each tile is a multiplier of measured ratios on the measured albedo, bound as map AND bumpMap; the lacquer is re-based to the plaster envelope so its flakes can be brighter than the red. The first pass at sixteen flakes per tile read as spots, not peel, and was cut to six; the first stone pass read as a barcode of streaks and was softened to blurred washes.
